title: Product of Array Except Self
keyIdea: answer[i] = (product of everything left of i) × (product of everything right of i). Fill res with left products in one pass, then sweep from the right with a running suffix product and multiply it in. No division, O(1) extra space.

approaches.name: Prefix and suffix arrays
approaches.idea: pref[i] = product left of i, suf[i] = product right of i, res[i] = pref[i] × suf[i].
approaches.why: Three linear passes; two extra arrays of size n.

approaches.name: Output array + running suffix
approaches.idea: res[i] = res[i−1] × nums[i−1] (left products). Then from the right: res[i] *= suffix; suffix *= nums[i].
approaches.why: Two passes. The output array doesn't count as extra space, and the right side is one variable.

quiz.q: Why not divide the total product by nums[i]?
options: It breaks when nums[i] is 0 (and the problem forbids division)

quiz.q: What does res hold after the first pass?
options: The product of everything to the left of each index

quiz.q: Why is it O(1) extra space?
options: res is the output; the right side is a single suffix variable
It uses no arrays at all
